Optional Neural Engine assist for convolutional models. Off by default: existing models, code and the `.knx` format work exactly as before.

## New

**Neural Engine assist** (`Model(path, ane=True)`, `kernix_model_set_ane(m, 1)`, `src/kernix_coreml.m`)
- KERNIX finds the parts of the graph that contain convolutions and builds a Core ML model for each one at run time, from the `.knx` already loaded. No separate Core ML file and no change to the export step.
- Output still comes from KERNIX: the API, the result buffer and everything outside those parts stay on the KERNIX path. RNNs, attention and embeddings never leave KERNIX.
- Compiles run in the background (0.1–0.3 s) once the same batch size arrives twice in a row, so no call waits for a compile.
- Each part is timed on both paths and keeps the faster one for that batch size. If Core ML fails, the part falls back to KERNIX for good.
- `trim()` also releases the Core ML models. `ane_info()` reports segments, compiles, Neural Engine runs and failures.
- New static library `libkernix_coreml.a` (installed by `install_mac.sh`) for C builds with `-DKERNIX_USE_COREML`. Needs macOS 13 or later; otherwise you get a warning and the normal path.

## Results (Apple M1, ResNet from README section 9, Python binding)

| | Batch 1 | Batch 64 | Peak memory added |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| KERNIX | 0.44 ms | 20.7–22.0 ms | |
| **KERNIX `ane=True`** | **0.17 ms** | **2.0–2.3 ms** | +10.8 / +14.3 MB |
| Core ML CPU+ANE alone | 0.28–0.31 ms | 1.53–1.61 ms | |

- Error with `ane=True` is 1.4e-3 (the Neural Engine computes in float16), against 4.5e-7 for the normal path. That is why it is off by default.
- LSTM, GPT and MLP are unchanged (no convolution).

## Verification

- 13 Neural Engine tests: matching outputs, fallback when a compile fails, closing while compiling, `trim`, calls from several threads. Also run under ASan.
- 17 PyTorch and 21 Keras reference models still match the original (about 1e-7 relative error excluding int8).
- Corrupted `.knx` fuzzing under ASan/UBSan: no memory errors.
